processes.title: Third-Party Order Processing
processes.memory_hook: We sell it; the vendor ships it.
processes.business_intent: Fulfill a customer order through an external supplier who ships directly to the customer.

control_plane.why: turns the sales item into third-party procurement
creates the purchase requisition and procurement linkage
feeds supplier dates/quantities back toward the sales order
decides what supplier event allows customer billing

data_hinges.changes: supplier delivery destination and purchasing documents
purchase requisition / purchase order and customer confirmation
sales-order confirmed dates and customer promise

impact_summary: No outbound delivery from your own plant in the direct-ship branch; procurement and billing become part of the customer-fulfillment chain.
constraints: The procurement item must stay linked to the originating sales-order item.
Changing or deleting items after procurement progresses can be restricted.
Supplier confirmation behavior depends on the selected variant.
lead_questions: Who owns the customer promise when the vendor misses the date?
What event makes the customer invoice legitimate?
Which changes must synchronize SD and MM?

processes.title: Purchase-to-Order / Order-Specific Procurement
processes.memory_hook: Buy for one customer, receive it, then deliver it.

sap_scope_items.label: Sales of Non-Stock Item with Order-Specific Procurement

processes.business_intent: Procure a product specifically for one sales-order item when the product should not satisfy unrelated demand.

control_plane.why: keeps procurement tied to one customer requirement
prevents the procured quantity from becoming general stock

data_hinges.changes: procurement account assignment and stock ownership context
procurement dates and downstream customer promise
when the sales item can realistically be delivered

impact_summary: Unlike direct third-party, the goods come into your controlled stock/process before customer delivery; the stock is still reserved for the specific order.
constraints: Order-specific stock is not interchangeable with normal unrestricted stock.
Procurement lead time becomes part of the sales promise.
lead_questions: Why is this PTO rather than TPO?
Can another sales order consume the procured stock?

processes.title: Sales Bill of Material / Sales Kit
processes.memory_hook: One sellable product can explode into a main item and components.
processes.business_intent: Sell a structured product while deciding whether pricing, inventory and delivery are controlled mainly by the main item or by its components.

control_plane.why: keeps processing mainly on the main item; in the classic model the components act as text items and are not delivery relevant
moves pricing, inventory and delivery processing to the component level
uses sales document type, item category group, item usage and higher-level item category to determine main and subitem behavior

control_plane.control: BOM explosion and higher-level item relationship
control_plane.why: creates the document structure and gives subitems their sales context

data_hinges.changes: which components appear in the sales order and in what ratio

data_hinges.data: item category group ERLA or LUMF
data_hinges.changes: whether the commercial and logistics control sits mainly on the main item or components
subitem item-category determination and follow-on behavior
whether the sales demand remains only a sales structure or also drives customer-specific production

impact_summary: A Sales BOM controls how a product structure is sold and executed in the sales document.
A Production BOM controls how a product is manufactured. The structures can be related, but they answer different business questions.
When an MTO strategy is active, the sales-order requirement can create customer-specific planning and production while the Sales BOM still controls the commercial item structure.
constraints: ERLA and LUMF are item category groups, not sales item categories.
Do not assume that a Sales BOM automatically means make-to-order production.
Main-item and subitem changes can affect pricing, delivery grouping, ATP, copying and document flow; test change behavior after the order already exists.
lead_questions: Where should pricing sit: main item or components?
Is this only a sales structure, or must the demand also trigger MTO production?
What should happen when the BOM changes after the sales order was created?

modes.title: Main-item processing
modes.memory: Price and control the sellable header; components mainly explain the structure.

modes.title: Component-level processing
modes.memory: Components carry the operational sales and delivery behavior.

relations.why: Main and subitem behavior depends on item-category determination.
With an MTO strategy, the sales-order requirement becomes customer-specific supply and production.
Assembly processing can create the production-side object directly from the sales order.

processes.title: Customer Consignment
processes.memory_hook: Our stock sits at the customer until they consume it.
processes.business_intent: Keep company-owned stock at a customer location and separate the physical move from the ownership/revenue event.

control_plane.why: distinguishes fill-up, issue, pick-up and return
identifies whose consignment stock is managed

data_hinges.changes: customer special stock and company valuated stock

impact_summary: Fill-up and pick-up move stock without changing ownership; issue and consignment return change ownership and therefore commercial treatment.
constraints: Consignment stock must be managed separately.
Availability checks differ between own plant stock and customer consignment stock.
lead_questions: Who owns the goods at this exact step?
Is billing expected because ownership changed or merely because stock moved?

modes.title: Issue
modes.memory: Customer consumes; ownership and billing start

modes.title: Return
modes.memory: Customer returns already-issued goods to consignment
